findings.title: Rounds.close: "2 on a stamp mismatch" is true for only one of three stamp mismatches
locations: src/CLI/Passes.jl:867: "Returns 0 when closed, 1 when a condition is unmet, 2 on a stamp mismatch."
src/CLI/Passes.jl:890: "(st[\"config_sha\"] == rec[\"config_sha\"] || latest_regrade) || push!(fails, \"config changed since open ...\")"
src/CLI/Passes.jl:891: "(st[\"tool_version\"] == rec[\"tool_version\"] || latest_regrade) || push!(fails, \"tool version moved (...) ...\")"
src/CLI/Passes.jl:892: "if st[\"tool_tree_sha\"] != rec[\"tool_tree_sha\"] && st[\"tool_version\"] == rec[\"tool_version\"] && !startswith(...) ... return 2"
findings.description: close()'s docstring states the exit contract as "0 when closed, 1 when a condition is unmet, 2 on a stamp mismatch", reading as if any stamp disagreement (config_sha, tool_version, tool_tree_sha) yields exit 2. The body only returns 2 for the tool_tree_sha-under-same-version anomaly (a moved tag). A changed config_sha or a moved tool_version is instead pushed onto `fails` and returns 1 like any other unmet condition.
findings.resolution_hint: Reword to: "2 only when the tool's tree hash moved under an unchanged version (a moved tag, abandon-only); a changed config_sha or tool_version is an ordinary refused condition (exit 1, fixed by --regrade)."

findings.title: Release.release: cites_round's closure test is narrower in the docstring than in the code
locations: src/CLI/Release.jl:44: "the `/check-docs` round opened at the latest `<ver>-rc.<n>` tag is closed by honored or adjudicated ids"
src/CLI/Release.jl:25: "get(e, \"closed_by\", nothing) in (\"honored\", \"adjudicated\", \"rescan\", \"seeded\") || String(id) in carried"
findings.description: The `release` docstring says the gating round must have every id "closed by honored or adjudicated ids", but `cites_round` (the function that actually performs this check) accepts four closure channels — honored, adjudicated, rescan, seeded — plus any id in the round's carried-forward set.
findings.resolution_hint: List all four closure channels plus the carried-id exemption, matching cites_round's actual `in ("honored","adjudicated","rescan","seeded")` test.

findings.title: Rounds.classify_lane omits the zero-findings/empty-checked path to :dead
locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl:305-309: "The status is `:dead` (absent, or — renamed to `<name>.rejected.json` beside itself — unparsable or invalid), `:rejected` ... `:empty` (zero findings, non-empty checked), `:truncated` (candidates_found > findings), or `:live`."
src/CLI/Rounds.jl:328: "(n == 0 && isempty(get(data, \"checked\", []))) && return (:dead, data, sha, \"zero findings AND empty checked[] — a dead lane, not a clean one\")"
findings.description: The docstring enumerates every path to :dead as only 'absent, or ... unparsable or invalid' (all renamed-to-.rejected cases). It never mentions the distinct branch where a schema-valid, correctly-named lane file with zero findings AND an empty checked[] is also :dead (not renamed) — exactly the RULE.TEST.MISSING_IS_FAILING mechanism.
findings.resolution_hint: Add a fourth :dead case: "or — not renamed — zero findings with an empty checked[] (a dead lane that never ran, not a clean one)."

findings.title: Rounds.seed_docs_corpus! has two distinct exit-2 paths but the docstring names only one
locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl:220: "Returns 0, or 2 when the catalogue plants nothing."
findings.description: The docstring's return contract describes only the isempty(plan) branch. A second, independent branch also returns 2 when the catalogue matched something but plant_files() only planted SOME of it — a materially different failure (partial planting) with its own message, never mentioned.
findings.resolution_hint: State both conditions: "Returns 0, or 2 when the catalogue matches nothing in the lane surfaces, or when some matched seeds fail to plant into the copied files."

findings.title: Install.cmd_install: "Returns 0 when both files are written" overstates the normal (no --dev-checkout) path
locations: src/CLI/Install.jl:38: "Returns 0 when both files are written, 2 when the Julia in use is below the floor, ..."
src/CLI/Install.jl:53-65: the `--dev-checkout` block (writes dev_pointer()) runs only `if haskey(o.values, "dev-checkout")`; the shim copy always runs
findings.description: In the common invocation `gbg install` with no `--dev-checkout`, only the shim file is ever written — dev_pointer() is skipped — and the function still returns 0, contradicting "Returns 0 when both files are written".
findings.resolution_hint: Split the claim: "Returns 0 when the shim is written (and, with --dev-checkout, the pointer too); 2 when ...".

findings.title: Git.changed_paths's docstring doesn't flag that an empty `paths` means UNRESTRICTED, not "no paths"
locations: src/CLI/Git.jl:128-133: "The files changed in a commit range under a set of paths ... `paths` — the paths the listing is restricted to."

src/CLI/Passes.jl:281-283: "# the diff is asked for the WHOLE tree: scoping it to the covered paths while the named set is not scoped at all ... touched = Set(Git.changed_paths(root, range, String[]))"
findings.description: changed_paths's docstring describes `paths` uniformly as restricting the listing. Passing an empty vector actually means NO restriction at all (git's `--` semantics) — the opposite of restricting — as the one caller's own comment has to explain because the function's docstring gives no warning.
findings.resolution_hint: Add: "an empty `paths` restricts to nothing being excluded — i.e. the WHOLE tree — not to zero files."

findings.title: Fleet's docstrings enumerate four row statuses; the code produces a fifth ("MISSING")
locations: src/CLI/Fleet.jl:7-9: "computes one row per consumer of `fleet.toml` — `OK`, `NOT-INITIALISED`, `BEHIND` or `RED` with a detail"
src/CLI/Fleet.jl:70: "push!(out, (name = c[\"name\"], pin = \"—\", status = \"MISSING\", detail = \"$(c[\"path\"]) does not exist\")); code = 2"
findings.description: Both the module docstring and Fleet.rows's docstring name exactly four status values. The code assigns a fifth literal, "MISSING", for a consumer whose path doesn't exist; the exit-2 behaviour is documented but this status string never appears in either enumeration.
findings.resolution_hint: Add MISSING to the enumerated statuses.

findings.title: Audit.audit_bank's "afterwards it prints the severity re-check" is conditional, not unconditional
locations: src/CLI/Audit.jl:19-21: "then runs [`Rounds.bank`](@ref); afterwards it prints the severity re-check Workflow call ..."
src/CLI/Audit.jl:54-72: `if !isempty(findings) ... println(...severity re-check...) else println(io, "audit-changes bank: no concern banked; ...") end`
findings.description: The docstring presents printing the severity re-check call as unconditional. The body only does this when the bank produced at least one finding; a clean bank prints a 'no concern banked' line instead and never renders the call.
findings.resolution_hint: Qualify: "when the bank produced any finding, it afterwards prints the severity re-check Workflow call; otherwise it reports a clean bank."
